```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(scales)
library(patchwork)
```

```{r}

palmtrees <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2025/2025-03-18/palmtrees.csv')

# cleaning names

palm <- palmtrees %>%
  clean_names()

```

## Basic Graph

```{r}


## Analysis Section
## Pareto Analysis of Genera

pareto_data <- palm %>%
  count(acc_genus) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 20) %>%
  mutate(
    cumulative = cumsum(n),
    cumulative_percent = cumulative / sum(n),
    acc_genus = fct_reorder(acc_genus, n)
  )

ggplot(pareto_data, aes(x = acc_genus)) +
  geom_col(aes(y = n), fill = "#2C7FB8") +
  geom_line(aes(y = cumulative_percent * max(n), group = 1),
            color = "darkred") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Count",
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / max(pareto_data$n),
                        name = "Cumulative %",
                        labels = percent)
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal()
```

## "The Economist" Style Graph

```{r}

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(forcats)

economist <- palm %>%
  count(acc_genus) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 15) %>%
  mutate(acc_genus = fct_reorder(acc_genus, n))

```

### Building a Minimal Base Plot

```{r}
ggplot(economist, aes(x = n, y = acc_genus)) +
  geom_col(fill = "grey80")
```

This is plain and quiet.

### Add Highlight (Top Genus in Red)

```{r}

economist <- economist %>%
  mutate(highlight = ifelse(row_number() == n(), "highlight", "normal"))

# Graphing it

ggplot(economist, aes(x = n, y = acc_genus, fill = highlight)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "normal" = "grey80",
    "highlight" = "#C0392B"
  )) +
  guides(fill = "none")
```

Now we have hierarchy.

### Economist Theme Styling

```{r}
economist_plot <- ggplot(economist, aes(x = n, y = acc_genus, fill = highlight)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "normal" = "grey80",
    "highlight" = "#C0392B"
  )) +
  
  labs(
    title = "A Small Number of Genera Dominate Observations",
    subtitle = "Top 15 genera account for most detections",
    x = "Number of Observations",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 16,
      margin = margin(b = 10)
    ),
    
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      color = "grey40",
      margin = margin(b = 15)
    ),
    
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    
    axis.text = element_text(color = "grey20"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 10))
  ) +
  annotate("rect", # adding the economist red headline
         xmin = -Inf,
         xmax = Inf,
         ymin = Inf,
         ymax = Inf,
         fill = "#C0392B")
```

### Creating the header then adding it to the above plot

```{r}
header <- ggplot() +
  
  # Create a rectangle that fills entire panel
  geom_rect(
    aes(xmin = 0, xmax = 1, ymin = 0, ymax = 1),
    fill = "#C0392B"
  ) +
  
  # Remove all axes and background elements
  theme_void()
```

```{r}
header / economist_plot + 
  plot_layout(heights = c(0.06, 1))
```

## Testing my own color brand

#### Setting up the data

```{r}
pareto_data <- palm %>%
  count(acc_genus) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 15) %>%
  mutate(cumulative = cumsum(n),
         cumulative_percent = cumulative / sum(n),
         acc_genus = forcats::fct_reorder(acc_genus, n))
```

#### Styled Chart 

```{r}
new_plot <- ggplot(pareto_data, aes(x = acc_genus)) +
  geom_col(aes(y = n),
           fill = midnight_narrative["linen"],
           color = midnight_narrative["midnight"],
           width = 0.8) +
  geom_col(data = pareto_data[which.max(pareto_data$n), ],
           aes(y = n),
           fill = midnight_narrative['coral']) +
  geom_line(aes(y = cumulative_percent * max(n), group = 1),
            color = midnight_narrative["sage"],
            linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(aes(y = cumulative_percent * max(n)),
             color = midnight_narrative["sage"],
             size = 2.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Count",
                     sec.axis = sec_axis(
                       ~ . / max(pareto_data$n),
                       name = "Cumulative %",
                       labels = scales::percent
                     )) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "A Small Number of Genera Dominate Observations",
       subtitle = "Cumulative percentage reveals concentration os detections",
       x = NULL) +
  theme_midnight_narrative()

new_plot
```
